mcqs.q: In this trial, robenacoxib in cats with degenerative joint disease-associated pain produced what outcome on owner-assessed disability vs placebo?
o: An improvement only in sedated cats
mcqs.e: Robenacoxib significantly decreased owner-assessed disability by ~49% at 6 weeks.

mcqs.q: How did adverse-effect frequency compare between robenacoxib and placebo groups?
mcqs.e: Adverse effect frequencies were similar across treatment groups.

mcqs.q: Besides disability, which outcomes significantly improved with robenacoxib at 6 weeks?
mcqs.e: Robenacoxib significantly improved owner-rated temperament and happiness at 6 weeks.

mcqs.q: What did this pilot study conclude about transdermal gabapentin in cats?
o: It is not absorbed through feline skin
It penetrates skin, is systemically absorbed, and may decrease pain
It is only absorbed when given IV
mcqs.e: Gabapentin penetrated feline skin in vitro, was systemically absorbed, and may decrease pain scores.

mcqs.q: At which timepoint were pain scores NO longer significantly different from predose?
mcqs.e: No difference in pain scores was seen from predose to day 8 (P = .3).

mcqs.q: Where was gabapentin detected in the sampled cats?
o: Only in vitro, never in vivo
mcqs.e: Gabapentin was identified in all samples collected.

mcqs.q: How did frunevetmab (anti-NGF antibody) compare to placebo for feline DJD pain?
o: Improved owner-rated mobility, supported by accelerometry
mcqs.e: Frunevetmab improved owner mobility ratings over placebo, corroborated by objective accelerometry.

mcqs.q: Did route of administration (SC vs IV) affect frunevetmab efficacy?
mcqs.e: No difference in efficacy was found between SC and IV administration routes.

mcqs.q: Most adverse events in the study were attributed to what?
mcqs.e: The majority of adverse events were dermatitis/alopecia related to the activity-monitor collars.

mcqs.q: In this pooled safety analysis, how did robenacoxib's adverse-event risk compare to placebo over 4-12 weeks?
mcqs.e: The number of cats with at least one AE did not differ significantly between robenacoxib and placebo.

mcqs.q: What serum change was noted with robenacoxib vs placebo?
o: Slightly higher creatinine without related clinical effects
mcqs.e: Serum creatinine was modestly higher with robenacoxib but no related adverse clinical effects were detected.

mcqs.q: In the subgroup with chronic kidney disease, robenacoxib's relative risk of an AE was:
mcqs.e: In CKD cats the relative risk was 1.09 (P = .61), not significantly increased.

mcqs.q: Comparing targeted local infiltrations during cat OVH, early postoperative pain scores were:
o: Only measurable in the dexamethasone group
mcqs.e: Early postoperative pain scores were similar across bupivacaine, BLE, dexamethasone, and meloxicam groups.

mcqs.q: At 3 hours post-recovery, which group had significantly lower pain scores?
mcqs.e: At 3 h the meloxicam group had significantly lower pain scores than the BLE group.

mcqs.q: How did pain scores at 1 h compare to 3 h post-recovery across groups?
mcqs.e: Overall pain scores 1 h post-recovery were significantly higher than at 3 h.

mcqs.q: What was found regarding correlation between mechanical thresholds and CMPS-Feline scores?
mcqs.e: There was no correlation between mechanical thresholds and CMPS-Feline scores.

mcqs.q: Comparing preoperative and postoperative mechanical thresholds (MT) measured in the surgical area, the study found:
o: Preoperative MT (340 g) were significantly higher than postoperative (233 g)
Postoperative MT were significantly higher than preoperative
MT could not be measured postoperatively
mcqs.e: Preoperative MT (340 g) were significantly higher than postoperatively (233 g; P = 0.001).

mcqs.q: Inter-observer agreement for postoperative CMPS-Feline scoring was described as:
mcqs.e: Inter-observer agreement was poor for the postoperative CMPS-Feline evaluations.

mcqs.q: After cat OVH, how did grapiprant compare with carprofen for early analgesia?
o: Grapiprant did not provide adequate analgesia in the first 3 h vs carprofen
Grapiprant better only at q12h dosing
mcqs.e: Grapiprant did not provide adequate analgesia during the first 3 h postoperatively compared with carprofen.

mcqs.q: Rescue analgesia requirement was highest in which group(s)?
mcqs.e: 67% of grapiprant cats needed rescue vs 18% of carprofen cats.

mcqs.q: Did giving grapiprant every 12 h instead of every 24 h add benefit?
mcqs.e: No benefit was observed by administering grapiprant every 12 h.

mcqs.q: In cats on propofol TIVA, dexmedetomidine produced what propofol-sparing effect?
mcqs.e: Dexmedetomidine produced a propofol-sparing effect of ~71-75% across the Dex groups.

mcqs.q: Which group most frequently required intraoperative rescue analgesia (fentanyl)?
mcqs.e: Rescue intraoperative analgesia was most frequent in the propofol-only (Prop) group.

mcqs.q: Which group had the worst anesthetic recovery quality scores?
mcqs.e: The Prop group scored the worst recovery quality (median 1).

mcqs.q: Comparing opioid-sparing (with buprenorphine) vs opioid-free anesthesia in cat OVH, rescue analgesia prevalence was:
mcqs.e: No opioid-sparing cats (0/13) needed rescue vs 5/14 opioid-free cats.

mcqs.q: What was concluded about opioid-free injectable anesthesia in this study?
o: Appropriate for some cats but a single IM buprenorphine dose ensured adequate analgesia
mcqs.e: Opioid-free anesthesia worked for some cats, but a single IM buprenorphine dose eliminated the need for rescue analgesia.

mcqs.q: Feline Grimace Scale scores in the opioid-free group at 1-2 h postoperatively were:
mcqs.e: FGS scores were higher than baseline at 1 and 2 h in the opioid-free group, but not in the opioid-sparing group.

mcqs.q: In anesthetized dogs given a noxious interdigital clamp, the respiratory Drive (VT/Ti) parameter:
o: Showed no change in any dog
Appeared to increase, mainly in dogs that did not move during a full 60 s stimulus
mcqs.e: Drive appeared to increase only in dogs that did not move and were clamped for the full 60 s.

mcqs.q: What happened to the Timing parameter after morphine administration?
mcqs.e: Timing seemed to increase after morphine administration.

mcqs.q: The authors' overall conclusion about Drive as a nociception monitor was that it:
o: Is a fully validated reliable monitor
Needs further in-depth study to determine sensitivity
mcqs.e: Drive needs further study to determine its sensitivity and precocity for monitoring acute nociception.

mcqs.q: After rabbit orchidectomy, the Rabbit Grimace Scale was found to be:
o: An effective tool for identifying when rabbits are painful
Useful only in NZW rabbits at 5 h
mcqs.e: Using behavior as the gold standard, the RbtGS effectively identified painful rabbits after orchidectomy.

mcqs.q: Which analgesic regimen reduced pain more effectively in Dutch belted rabbits?
o: High-dose meloxicam (0.6 mg/kg) plus local anesthetic
mcqs.e: High-dose meloxicam combined with lidocaine/bupivacaine reduced pain more than low-dose meloxicam alone.

mcqs.q: Pain-associated behaviors significantly increased at which postoperative timepoints?
mcqs.e: Rabbits showed significant increases in pain behaviors at 1 and 5 h post-surgery.

mcqs.q: Adding reflective blankets and wool socks during canine celiotomy resulted in:
o: Significantly higher esophageal temperatures than routine support alone
mcqs.e: The supplemental group maintained significantly higher esophageal temperatures than the control group.

mcqs.q: The lowest temperature in the supplemental group, adjusted for covariates, was higher than control by approximately:
mcqs.e: The adjusted lowest temperature was significantly higher by 0.8 C in the supplemental group.

mcqs.q: The authors characterized supplemental reflective blankets/wool socks as:
o: An affordable passive heat-support method to minimize perioperative hypothermia
mcqs.e: It is described as an affordable adjunctive passive heat-support method to minimize perioperative hypothermia.
